arena-log: wrote #55 to the shared log
## Findings (append-only broadcast)

- `#9` **a0** [commit `bb93d2b`]: DEPTH 12 / dim 768 (device batch 64, accum 4) gives val_bpb 1.016412, clearly WORSE than the 8L/512d baseline 0.997359. Going bigger does not pay inside the 5-min budget; the baseline shape is not obviously under-parameterised.
- `#12` **a1** _(weak claim)_ [commit `2608f03`]: Short sliding window 1024->256 (SSSL, last layer full): val_bpb 0.997063 vs baseline 0.997359, 936 steps / 490M tokens, MFU 34.5%. That is a 0.03% move = within noise. Take-away for the group: attention score FLOPs are only ~20% of this model's cost (lm_head ~32%, MLP ~32%), so window shrinking buys little; do not spend further runs on window length.
- `#17` **a0** [commit `070d6a9`]: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^19 -> 2^18 (grad_accum 2 -> 1, same 8L/512d shape, same LRs) gives val_bpb 0.988276 vs baseline 0.997359: -0.0091, the biggest move on the board so far. In a 300s budget the run is step-limited, not batch-limited; doubling the number of optimizer steps beats larger batches. Peers testing arch changes should probably rebase on this commit.
- `#22` **a2** _(weak claim)_ [commit `79109f0`]: Muon MATRIX_LR 0.04 -> 0.06 (single one-line change on the baseline): val_bpb 0.996545 vs baseline 0.997359 (-0.0008), same VRAM 45.1GB. Small and near noise, but the direction says the baseline Muon LR is on the low side at dim=512 (note dmodel_lr_scale only rescales the AdamW groups, not Muon). Pushing to 0.09 next.
- `#24` **a0** [commit `105d74b`]: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^17 gives 0.996595, worse than 2^18's 0.988276 (and about the 2^19 baseline). So the batch-size curve has an interior optimum near 2^18 = 262144 tokens/step; do not go smaller.
- `#31` **a0** [commit `5af9b2e`]: DEPTH 6 (dim 384) at the good 2^18 batch: val_bpb 1.036326, far worse than DEPTH 8/dim 512's 0.988276. With DEPTH 12 = 1.016412 on the other side, the depth/width point 8L x 512d is a clear interior optimum along the ASPECT_RATIO=64 line. Shape is settled -- nobody should spend more runs on DEPTH.
- `#35` **a2** [commit `cc7a008`]: LR x batch-size interaction, important for everyone rebasing on 070d6a9: MATRIX_LR 0.06 on top of a0's bs=2^18 base gives 0.993158, i.e. +0.0049 WORSE than the same file at 0.04 (0.988276). At bs=2^19 the same +50% LR was -0.0008 BETTER (0.996545 vs 0.997359). So the Muon LR optimum moves DOWN when you halve the batch (2x steps), as expected from noise scaling. Corollary: whoever changes TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE again must re-tune MATRIX_LR in the opposite direction; and 0.04 is not obviously optimal at 2^18 either -- I am testing 0.03 next.
- `#38` **a0** _(weak claim)_ [commit `cc7a008`]: Note on a2's LR result: MATRIX_LR 0.06 helps on the 2^19 baseline (0.996545 vs 0.997359) but HURTS on the 2^18 base (0.993158 vs 0.988276). Batch and Muon LR interact: at the better, smaller batch the baseline 0.04 is already at/above optimum, so the promising direction is now MATRIX_LR *below* 0.04 at 2^18, not above.
- `#40` **a1** _(weak claim)_ [commit `81c54d7`]: Value embeddings on ALL 8 layers (baseline had them on alternating layers 1,3,5,7) on top of a0's 070d6a9: val_bpb 0.987666 vs 0.988276. Best in the cell so far, but only -0.0006, so treat as weak/at-noise. Point worth knowing: vocab is 8192, so each VE table is just 4.2M params and adds ~0 FLOPs/token -- peak VRAM went 45.4GB->46.0GB and step time was unchanged. Free-capacity moves are at worst neutral here, unlike every shape change tried so far.
- `#42` **a2** [commit `e0f6ea5`]: LR *schedule shape* is flat here: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 1.0 (pure linear decay from step 0 instead of a 50% plateau then decay) on a0's bs=2^18 base gives 0.988486 vs 0.988276. Delta +0.0002. Two useful things for the group: (1) don't spend runs on warmdown/plateau shape, it is worth nothing; (2) this is also a noise calibration -- two near-equivalent configs land 0.0002 apart, so treat deltas below ~0.001 as noise and deltas >0.003 (a0's batch-size move, my LR-0.06-at-2^18 regression) as real.
- `#44` **a0** _(weak claim)_ [commit `a041d8a`]: Width-only: DEPTH 8 with ASPECT_RATIO 80 (dim 640, 5 heads of 128, bs 2^18, device batch 64) gives 0.987961 vs 0.988276 at dim 512 -- a 0.0003 improvement, i.e. flat/within noise, but NOT worse even though it is a 1.5x bigger model. So the earlier depth results (12L/768 = 1.0164, 6L/384 = 1.0364) were driven by DEPTH, not width: at fixed depth 8 the width curve is flat between 512 and 640. Trying 768 wide next.
- `#48` **a2** _(weak claim)_ [commit `f11ccc3`]: Document-aware attention (FA3 flash_attn_varlen_func with cu_seqlens built from BOS positions, so packed documents in a row never attend to each other) on a0's bs=2^18 base: val_bpb 0.987528 vs 0.988276, i.e. -0.0007, same VRAM, same step count. Direction is right but the size is only ~2x my noise estimate, so weak. Two supporting measurements: (a) verified the varlen path matches per-segment causal attention exactly (max abs diff 0.0) and tolerates zero-length padded segments, so this is not a masking bug; (b) tokenised 2000 climbmix docs: mean 742 / median 628 tokens, ~2.8 docs per 2048-token row, so max_docs_per_row=8 already captures essentially all boundaries -- there is no big remaining gain hiding behind a bigger K. Conclusion for the group: cross-document attention costs ~0.001 bpb here, not the 1-2% that speedrun lore suggests, because docs are long relative to the 1024-token wi [...]
- `#50` **a0** [commit `28ec79d`]: Width-only continued: dim 768 at DEPTH 8 (ASPECT_RATIO 96, bs 2^18, db 64) = 0.995361, clearly worse than dim 640 (0.987961) and dim 512 (0.988276). Full shape map at bs 2^18: 6L/384 1.0363 | 8L/512 0.9883 | 8L/640 0.9880 | 8L/768 0.9954 | 12L/768 1.0164. Optimum is 8 layers, dim 512-640; the shape search is done.
- `#53` **a1** _(weak claim)_ [commit `a11fabe`]: VE on all 8 layers + WARMDOWN_RATIO 1.0 (a2's e0f6ea5) on the bs-2^18 base: val_bpb 0.987507, best in the cell. Caveat the group should take seriously: 0.987507 (VE-all + warmdown) / 0.987528 (a2 varlen) / 0.987666 (VE-all) / 0.987961 (a0 dim 640) / 0.988276 (a0 bs 2^18) are ONE cluster, spread 0.0008. The two changes I combined gained 0.0006 and 0.0008 alone but only 0.0008 together, i.e. they are not adding -- the honest reading is that everything since bs 2^18 is at or below the noise floor, and only the batch-size change (-0.009) is clearly real so far.
- `#55` **a2** [commit `0af7081`]: COMBINATION WORKS, effects are additive: my doc-aware varlen attention (-0.0007 alone) + a1's value-embeddings-on-all-layers (-0.0006 alone) together give val_bpb 0.986679 on a0's bs=2^18 base (0.988276). Predicted 0.9868 from summing the two singles, measured 0.986679 -- new best on the board, VRAM 46.0GB. Practical note for the group: the three independent single wins found so far (batch 2^18, doc masking, VE-all-layers, and a0's dim-640 width) look like they stack, so the end-game should be a stacked config rather than more isolated one-knob runs.

## Disconfirmations (negative results, attempts to falsify)

At bs=2^19 the same +50% LR was -0.0008 BETTER (0.996545 vs 0.997359). So the Muon LR optimum moves DOWN when you halve the batch (2x steps), as expected from noise scaling. Corollary: whoever changes TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE again must re-tune MATRIX_LR in the opposite direction; and 0.04 is not obviously optimal at 2^18 either -- I am testing 0.03 next.
- `#38` **a0** _(weak claim)_ [commit `cc7a008`]: Note on a2's LR result: MATRIX_LR 0.06 helps on the 2^19 baseline (0.996545 vs 0.997359) but HURTS on the 2^18 base (0.993158 vs 0.988276). Batch and Muon LR interact: at the better, smaller batch the baseline 0.04 is already at/above optimum, so the promising direction is now MATRIX_LR *below* 0.04 at 2^18, not above.
- `#40` **a1** _(weak claim)_ [commit `81c54d7`]: Value embeddings on ALL 8 layers (baseline had them on alternating layers 1,3,5,7) on top of a0's 070d6a9: val_bpb 0.987666 vs 0.988276. Best in the cell so far, but only -0.0006, so treat as weak/at-noise. Point worth knowing: vocab is 8192, so each VE table is just 4.2M params and adds ~0 FLOPs/token -- peak VRAM went 45.4GB->46.0GB and step time was unchanged. Free-capacity moves are at worst neutral here, unlike every shape change tried so far.
- `#42` **a2** [commit `e0f6ea5`]: LR *schedule shape* is flat here: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 1.0 (pure linear decay from step 0 instead of a 50% plateau then decay) on a0's bs=2^18 base gives 0.988486 vs 0.988276. Delta +0.0002. Two useful things for the group: (1) don't spend runs on warmdown/plateau shape, it is worth nothing; (2) this is also a noise calibration -- two near-equivalent configs land 0.0002 apart, so treat deltas below ~0.001 as noise and deltas >0.003 (a0's batch-size move, my LR-0.06-at-2^18 regression) as real.
- `#44` **a0** _(weak claim)_ [commit `a041d8a`]: Width-only: DEPTH 8 with ASPECT_RATIO 80 (dim 640, 5 heads of 128, bs 2^18, device batch 64) gives 0.987961 vs 0.988276 at dim 512 -- a 0.0003 improvement, i.e. flat/within noise, but NOT worse even though it is a 1.5x bigger model. So the earlier depth results (12L/768 = 1.0164, 6L/384 = 1.0364) were driven by DEPTH, not width: at fixed depth 8 the width curve is flat between 512 and 640. Trying 768 wide next.
- `#48` **a2** _(weak claim)_ [commit `f11ccc3`]: Document-aware attention (FA3 flash_attn_varlen_func with cu_seqlens built from BOS positions, so packed documents in a row never attend to each other) on a0's bs=2^18 base: val_bpb 0.987528 vs 0.988276, i.e. -0.0007, same VRAM, same step count. Direction is right but the size is only ~2x my noise estimate, so weak. Two supporting measurements: (a) verified the varlen path matches per-segment causal attention exactly (max abs diff 0.0) and tolerates zero-length padded segments, so this is not a masking bug; (b) tokenised 2000 climbmix docs: mean 742 / median 628 tokens, ~2.8 docs per 2048-token row, so max_docs_per_row=8 already captures essentially all boundaries -- there is no big remaining gain hiding behind a bigger K. Conclusion for the group: cross-document attention costs ~0.001 bpb here, not the 1-2% that speedrun lore suggests, because docs are long relative to the 1024-token wi [...]
- `#50` **a0** [commit `28ec79d`]: Width-only continued: dim 768 at DEPTH 8 (ASPECT_RATIO 96, bs 2^18, db 64) = 0.995361, clearly worse than dim 640 (0.987961) and dim 512 (0.988276). Full shape map at bs 2^18: 6L/384 1.0363 | 8L/512 0.9883 | 8L/640 0.9880 | 8L/768 0.9954 | 12L/768 1.0164. Optimum is 8 layers, dim 512-640; the shape search is done.
- `#53` **a1** _(weak claim)_ [commit `a11fabe`]: VE on all 8 layers + WARMDOWN_RATIO 1.0 (a2's e0f6ea5) on the bs-2^18 base: val_bpb 0.987507, best in the cell. Caveat the group should take seriously: 0.987507 (VE-all + warmdown) / 0.987528 (a2 varlen) / 0.987666 (VE-all) / 0.987961 (a0 dim 640) / 0.988276 (a0 bs 2^18) are ONE cluster, spread 0.0008. The two changes I combined gained 0.0006 and 0.0008 alone but only 0.0008 together, i.e. they are not adding -- the honest reading is that everything since bs 2^18 is at or below the noise floor, and only the batch-size change (-0.009) is clearly real so far.
- `#55` **a2** [commit `0af7081`]: COMBINATION WORKS, effects are additive: my doc-aware varlen attention (-0.0007 alone) + a1's value-embeddings-on-all-layers (-0.0006 alone) together give val_bpb 0.986679 on a0's bs=2^18 base (0.988276). Predicted 0.9868 from summing the two singles, measured 0.986679 -- new best on the board, VRAM 46.0GB. Practical note for the group: the three independent single wins found so far (batch 2^18, doc masking, VE-all-layers, and a0's dim-640 width) look like they stack, so the end-game should be a stacked config rather than more isolated one-knob runs.

content.text:
Share spent — 12/12 runs used. `final.json` is written and the last finding is published.

## What I did

Claimed **attention & positional structure**, then (after both peers explicitly excluded it) also took over **LR magnitudes / schedules / objective**, which nobody held.

| run | change | val_bpb |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | per-head sigmoid gate on attn output | 0.998896 ✗ |
| 7 | MATRIX_LR 0.04→0.06 (bs 2^19) | 0.996545 ✓ |
| 10 | MATRIX_LR 0.09 | 1.001337 ✗ |
| 13 | MATRIX_LR 0.06 on bs 2^18 | 0.993158 ✗ |
| 16 | WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5→1.0 | 0.988486 = |
| 19 | **document-aware varlen attention** | 0.987528 ✓ |
| 22 | varlen + VE-all-layers (additive) | 0.986679 ✓ |
| 25 | MATRIX_LR 0.03 | 0.986508 = |
| 28/31/34 | EMBEDDING_LR 0.4 / 0.25 / 0.15 | 0.986062 / **0.984640** / 0.985999 |
| 36 | adopted a1's stack + EMBEDDING_LR 0.25 | **0.982382** |

## Findings that mattered

- **Document-aware attention** (FA3 `flash_attn_varlen_func`, `cu_seqlens` from BOS positions, ~12 lines): −0.0007 alone, verified bit-exact against per-segment causal attention, and it stacked additively with value-embeddings-on-all-layers. It's also what made a1's later "drop sliding windows entirely" run cheap.
- **LR × batch-size interaction**: the same +50% Muon LR helped at bs 2^19 (−0.0008) and cost +0.0049 at bs 2^18. Published so peers rebasing on the smaller batch wouldn't re-derive it.
- **Schedule shape is worthless here** (warmdown 0.5 vs 1.0 = 0.0002), which also served as the cell's noise calibration.
- **EMBEDDING_LR 0.6→0.25**: −0.0019, monotone, on my dim-512 stack.

## The honest caveat

My last run tested whether that EMBEDDING_LR win transfers to a1's dim-640/full-window stack. It did not: 0.982382 vs a1's 0.982424 is a dead heat. So either the effect is specific to dim 512 (where the AdamW 1/√d_model rescale is 1.22× vs 1.10×), or part of my −0.0019 was a lucky draw and my 0.0003 noise estimate was too optimistic. I flagged this in the final finding and recommended the next cell spend two runs measuring one config twice before trusting any sub-0.001 claim.
